assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational framework connecting collateral constraints, asset prices, and macroeconomic fluctuations, with enduring influence on macro-finance.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the central collateral-credit-cycle mechanism; Gertler made major contributions to the financial-accelerator formulation and its macroeconomic use.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been deeply absorbed into theory and policy-oriented macroeconomics and were especially tested by subsequent financial crises.
uncertainties: The proposed umbrella contains closely related but distinct models, making the exact allocation of credit difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed modern trade theory and the analysis of trade gains, selection, and distributional consequences.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical heterogeneous-firm model, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established, extensively extended, and central in contemporary quantitative trade research.
uncertainties: The wider literature has many contributors, so a three-person attribution remains necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods gave empirical economics a broadly usable solution to persistent endogeneity and unobserved-heterogeneity problems.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are directly associated with the landmark estimator, with Blundell and Bond central to its system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These methods have had decades of extensive use, scrutiny, and refinement across applied economics.
uncertainties: Its widespread use has also exposed important finite-sample and instrument-proliferation limitations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining supplied a canonical strategic foundation for bargaining outcomes and stimulated a large theoretical and applied literature.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is the indispensable originator of the alternating-offers model; Wolinsky and Binmore made influential related contributions to bargaining and markets.
assessment.maturity: The theory is a durable part of the core game-theory curriculum and has generated sustained work over many decades.
uncertainties: The relative fit of the additional proposed laureates to the central alternating-offers discovery needs careful delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal-rigidity theory and the New Keynesian framework reshaped the analysis of monetary policy and inflation stabilization.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's price-setting device, Woodford's monetary theory, and Gertler's macroeconomic formulations are central, though the listed contribution spans many major researchers.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been dominant in research and policy analysis for decades, with abundant empirical and institutional engagement.
uncertainties: The candidate's broad formulation makes a limited laureate set especially difficult to justify cleanly.
The empirical adequacy of particular New Keynesian specifications remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation program made within-country resource allocation a central quantitative explanation for cross-country productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow supplied a highly influential empirical-quantitative framework, with Restuccia a principal contributor to the broader mechanism and literature.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a large body of measurement, theory, and policy research over a substantial period.
uncertainties: Inference from revenue productivity to distortions is model-dependent and alternative mechanisms can produce similar patterns.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on tasks, technology, and trade shocks materially changed understanding of wage inequality and local labor-market adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Dorn developed influential task and polarization analyses, while Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are jointly central to the China-shock evidence.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been repeatedly studied and have strongly influenced labor, trade, and public-policy research.
uncertainties: Separating technology, trade, and institutional causes of labor-market change remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models brought household distributions and marginal-propensity heterogeneity into the analysis of aggregate stabilization policy.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are the clear core contributors to the modern HANK framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has quickly become central to modern macroeconomic research and policy analysis, though it is younger than the leading candidates.
uncertainties: Its relatively recent development leaves less time for long-run assessment.
Quantitative conclusions depend on modeling and measurement choices.
